fruits.extendedStory: Gothic builders shaped these walls, with pointed arches and tall windows. The cellar holds something stranger: a barrel that Elector Carl Theodor had built. It was made to hold 220,000 litres. Someone had to watch over it, and that job went to a court steward called Perkeo. His real name was Clemens Pankert, and he came to Heidelberg in 1718.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Gotische Baumeister formten diese Mauern, mit Spitzbögen und hohen Fenstern. Im Keller steht etwas Seltsameres: ein Fass, das Kurfürst Carl Theodor bauen ließ. Es fasst 220.000 Liter. Jemand musste darauf aufpassen, und diese Aufgabe bekam ein Hofmeister namens Perkeo. Er hieß eigentlich Clemens Pankert und kam 1718 nach Heidelberg.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Gothic builders shaped these walls, with pointed arches and tall windows. The cellar holds something stranger: a barrel that Elector Carl Theodor had built. It was made to hold 220,000 litres. Someone had to watch over it, and that job went to a court steward called Perkeo. His real name was Clemens Pankert, and he came to Heidelberg in 1718.

localizedStory.de: Das Schloss liegt 213 Meter hoch, und im Keller steht ein Fass für 220.000 Liter.
localizedStory.en: The castle stands 213 metres up, and its cellar holds a barrel built to hold 220,000 litres.

fruits.name: Heidelberger Schloss
fruits.story: The castle stands 213 metres up, and its cellar holds a barrel built to hold 220,000 litres.

fruits.extendedStory: Walk along the outside wall and look between the buttresses. Small shops are wedged into the gaps there, and they have been for centuries. Inside, a wall once ran across the church from 1706 to 1936. The nave belonged to the protestants and the choir to the catholics, two congregations under one roof. Up on the galleries stood the old collegiate library, later swollen by elector Ludwig III's books.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Geh an der Außenwand entlang und schau zwischen die Strebepfeiler. Dort stecken kleine Läden in den Lücken, und das seit Jahrhunderten. Drinnen lief von 1706 bis 1936 eine Mauer quer durch die Kirche. Das Langhaus gehörte den Protestanten, der Chor den Katholiken, zwei Gemeinden unter einem Dach. Auf den Emporen stand die alte Stiftsbibliothek, später erweitert um die Bücher Kurfürst Ludwigs III.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Walk along the outside wall and look between the buttresses. Small shops are wedged into the gaps there, and they have been for centuries. Inside, a wall once ran across the church from 1706 to 1936. The nave belonged to the protestants and the choir to the catholics, two congregations under one roof. Up on the galleries stood the old collegiate library, later swollen by elector Ludwig III's books.

localizedStory.de: Der Bau dieser Kirche begann 1398, und sie trägt den Namen des Heiligen Geistes.
localizedStory.en: Work on this church began in 1398, and it carries the name of the Holy Spirit.

fruits.name: Heiliggeistkirche
fruits.story: Work on this church began in 1398, and it carries the name of the Holy Spirit.

fruits.extendedStory: Seven bridges stood here before this one, and all seven were destroyed. Ice carried several of them off down the river. The stone bridge that finally held is 200 metres long and rests on nine arches. At the town end look for the brass monkey holding up a mirror. It is an old joke: before you laugh at anyone crossing, take a look at yourself.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Sieben Brücken standen hier vor dieser, und alle sieben wurden zerstört. Mehrere trug das Eis den Fluss hinunter. Die steinerne, die endlich hielt, ist 200 Meter lang und ruht auf neun Bögen. Am Stadtende sitzt ein Affe aus Bronze und hält einen Spiegel hoch. Das ist ein alter Scherz: Bevor du über jemanden lachst, schau dich selbst an.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Seven bridges stood here before this one, and all seven were destroyed. Ice carried several of them off down the river. The stone bridge that finally held is 200 metres long and rests on nine arches. At the town end look for the brass monkey holding up a mirror. It is an old joke: before you laugh at anyone crossing, take a look at yourself.

localizedStory.de: Kurfürst Karl Theodor eröffnete diese Brücke 1788, und sie trägt bis heute seinen Namen.
localizedStory.en: Elector Karl Theodor opened this bridge in 1788, and it still carries his name.

fruits.name: Alte Brücke
fruits.story: Elector Karl Theodor opened this bridge in 1788, and it still carries his name.

fruits.extendedStory: Boats used to tie up where the trams now turn. A harbour basin lay here from 1847 to 1874, dug for the growing traffic on the river. Once it was filled in, the open ground became a square. It was given Bismarck's name on 3 November 1875, for his sixtieth birthday. A bust of him by Adolf von Donndorf still stands in the garden at the middle.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Wo heute die Bahnen wenden, machten früher Schiffe fest. Von 1847 bis 1874 lag hier ein Hafenbecken, gegraben für den wachsenden Verkehr auf dem Fluss. Als man es zuschüttete, wurde aus der freien Fläche ein Platz. Bismarcks Namen bekam er am 3. November 1875, zu dessen sechzigstem Geburtstag. Eine Büste von Adolf von Donndorf steht noch im Garten in der Mitte.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Boats used to tie up where the trams now turn. A harbour basin lay here from 1847 to 1874, dug for the growing traffic on the river. Once it was filled in, the open ground became a square. It was given Bismarck's name on 3 November 1875, for his sixtieth birthday. A bust of him by Adolf von Donndorf still stands in the garden at the middle.

localizedStory.de: Hier lagen früher Schiffe im Winter. Der Platz wurde 1877 auf dem alten Hafen eröffnet und trägt den Namen Otto von Bismarcks.
localizedStory.en: Boats once spent the winter here. The square opened in 1877 on the old harbour and carries Otto von Bismarck's name.

fruits.name: Bismarckplatz
fruits.story: Boats once spent the winter here. The square opened in 1877 on the old harbour and carries Otto von Bismarck's name.

fruits.extendedStory: Josef Durm's building on the Plöck opened in 1905. Behind its sandstone front the library keeps one book people come a long way to see. The Codex Manesse runs to 426 parchment leaves and carries songs by 140 poets. It was written down when those songs were already old. A library is a strange sort of landmark: the treasure is inside, and it is paper.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Josef Durms Bau an der Plöck wurde 1905 eröffnet. Hinter der Sandsteinfassade bewahrt die Bibliothek ein Buch, für das Leute weit reisen. Der Codex Manesse umfasst 426 Pergamentblätter mit Liedern von 140 Dichtern. Aufgeschrieben wurde er, als diese Lieder schon alt waren. Eine Bibliothek ist ein seltsames Wahrzeichen: Der Schatz liegt drinnen, und er ist aus Papier.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Josef Durm's building on the Plöck opened in 1905. Behind its sandstone front the library keeps one book people come a long way to see. The Codex Manesse runs to 426 parchment leaves and carries songs by 140 poets. It was written down when those songs were already old. A library is a strange sort of landmark: the treasure is inside, and it is paper.

localizedStory.de: Josef Durm baute diese Bibliothek 1901 im eklektizistischen Stil — ältere Formen, geliehen und gemischt.
localizedStory.en: Josef Durm built this library in 1901 in an eclectic style — older shapes borrowed and mixed together.

fruits.name: Universitätsbibliothek
fruits.story: Josef Durm built this library in 1901 in an eclectic style — older shapes borrowed and mixed together.

fruits.extendedStory: Before this was a market square, a hospital stood here. The Heilig-Geist-Spital served the sick from the 13th century until 1557. That year the town council had it pulled down to make room for a market. Look at the paving: the outline of its vanished chapel is marked in the stones. When a car park was dug underneath in 1986, about 270 of some 800 graves were examined.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Bevor hier ein Marktplatz war, stand hier ein Spital. Das Heilig-Geist-Spital versorgte die Kranken vom 13. Jahrhundert bis 1557, als der Stadtrat es für einen Markt abreißen ließ. Schau aufs Pflaster: Der Grundriss der verschwundenen Kapelle ist in den Steinen markiert. Beim Bau der Tiefgarage 1986 untersuchte man rund 270 von etwa 800 Gräbern.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Before this was a market square, a hospital stood here. The Heilig-Geist-Spital served the sick from the 13th century until 1557. That year the town council had it pulled down to make room for a market. Look at the paving: the outline of its vanished chapel is marked in the stones. When a car park was dug underneath in 1986, about 270 of some 800 graves were examined.

localizedStory.de: Schau zur Kornmarktmadonna auf ihrem Brunnen — die Stadt datiert sie auf das 18. Jahrhundert.
localizedStory.en: Look up at the Kornmarkt Madonna on her fountain — the city dates her to the 18th century.

fruits.name: Kornmarkt
fruits.story: Look up at the Kornmarkt Madonna on her fountain — the city dates her to the 18th century.

fruits.extendedStory: Friedrich Ebert was born in Heidelberg on 4 February 1871. He did not start out in politics. Between 1885 and 1888 he learned the saddler's trade, working leather with his hands. From 1919 until his death in 1925 he was president of the German republic. The square carries his name in the town where he grew up.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Friedrich Ebert wurde am 4. Februar 1871 in Heidelberg geboren. Er begann nicht in der Politik. Zwischen 1885 und 1888 lernte er das Handwerk des Sattlers und arbeitete mit den Händen im Leder. Von 1919 bis zu seinem Tod 1925 war er Reichspräsident der deutschen Republik. Der Platz trägt seinen Namen in der Stadt, in der er aufwuchs.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Friedrich Ebert was born in Heidelberg on 4 February 1871. He did not start out in politics. Between 1885 and 1888 he learned the saddler's trade, working leather with his hands. From 1919 until his death in 1925 he was president of the German republic. The square carries his name in the town where he grew up.

localizedStory.de: Der Platz ist nach Friedrich Ebert benannt, der hier in Heidelberg geboren wurde.
localizedStory.en: The square is named for Friedrich Ebert, who was born right here in Heidelberg.

fruits.name: Friedrich-Ebert-Platz
fruits.story: The square is named for Friedrich Ebert, who was born right here in Heidelberg.

fruits.extendedStory: Elector Karl Ludwig paid for this church in 1661, and that was the point of it. The town's Lutheran families had no building of their own, and he gave them one. In a century when rulers often forced one faith on everybody, that counted as tolerance. Karl Hermann Behaghel drew the plans. The name means providence, the idea of being looked after.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Kurfürst Karl Ludwig bezahlte diese Kirche 1661, und genau darum ging es. Die lutherischen Familien der Stadt hatten kein eigenes Haus, und er gab ihnen eines. In einem Jahrhundert, in dem Herrscher oft allen einen Glauben aufzwangen, galt das als Duldung. Karl Hermann Behaghel entwarf den Bau. Der Name meint die Vorsehung, den Gedanken, behütet zu sein.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Elector Karl Ludwig paid for this church in 1661, and that was the point of it. The town's Lutheran families had no building of their own, and he gave them one. In a century when rulers often forced one faith on everybody, that counted as tolerance. Karl Hermann Behaghel drew the plans. The name means providence, the idea of being looked after.

localizedStory.de: Kurfürst Karl Ludwig ließ diese Kirche 1661 bauen, damit die lutherische Gemeinde einen eigenen Platz hatte.
localizedStory.en: Elector Karl Ludwig had this church built in 1661 so the town's Lutheran families had a place of their own.

fruits.name: Providenzkirche
fruits.story: Elector Karl Ludwig had this church built in 1661 so the town's Lutheran families had a place of their own.
